A write gets staged, and right after that, the whole job goes down, before anything confirms it's done.
Is that staged write gone for good, duplicated somewhere, or neither of those?
answer: Neither one, and that's the whole point of staging it first.
It was already safely saved before anything went wrong.
Recovery just needs to notice that and finish the one step still left undone.

lines: Here's the shape that makes that safe: durable well before it's ever visible to anyone.
A crash landing in between those two moments changes nothing about the eventual outcome.
Recovery comes along, finds exactly what was left staged, and finishes it, exactly once.
There's a second way to get the same safety, with no staging step involved at all.
Give every write an id computed the same way every single time from its own contents.
Send that same write again, and it simply lands on top of itself, not beside it.
One detail decides whether any of this actually holds together end to end.
Where exactly does the record of how far along you've gotten get saved?
Save it anywhere separate from the write itself, and the old gap is right back open.
Worth reasoning through once more before this reveal settles it.
Every mechanism described so far can be working exactly as intended, and this can still fail.
Name one real, specific way that happens.
answer: A few genuinely different things can each do it on their own.
A retry that quietly computes something different than the first attempt did is one.
Something no database can ever undo, or a clock set wrong in just one place, are two more.

lines: A retry that comes out differently than the original breaks the whole premise underneath it.
Something that reaches outside any database entirely simply can't be rolled back by one.
And a clock set too tight throws away a perfectly good write before it ever lands.
Every number shown in this reel came from one real run, happening just now, of this topic's own toy models.
The crash that lost nothing and duplicated nothing.
The retry that quietly became one single row, and the misconfigured run that lost every write it touched.
So: stage first and finalize later, or write by a repeatable id either one gets you there.
Keep the record of progress glued to the write it describes, not off on its own somewhere.
And remember that a few specific, ordinary things can still undo every bit of it.
